prompt: A résumé-screening assistant has lower interview recommendations for candidates from one language group. The base model and prompt are identical for all users. What should the team inspect next?

options.text: Only the model’s overall accuracy, since a single shared prompt rules out pipeline bias.
Trace data, extraction, examples, and routing by group.
The output wording alone, replacing every group label with a neutral term.
The provider’s general safety statement, then close the investigation if no bias is disclosed.

feedback.reason: Equal prompts do not imply equal outcomes; differences can enter through data, examples, extraction, thresholds, and downstream routes.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Fairness investigation should inspect the complete pipeline and compare relevant outcomes across appropriately defined groups.
details.scenarioApplication: Equal prompts do not imply equal outcomes; differences can enter through data, examples, extraction, thresholds, and downstream routes.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Group comparisons need suitable data, privacy controls, and careful interpretation; correlation alone does not establish cause.
details.errorCorrection: Measure comparable cases at the suspected stage; neither a pooled score nor a shared model establishes equal treatment.
details.transfer: Trace where disparities appear before choosing a corrective intervention.

messages.text: Overall accuracy can hide group differences; a shared prompt does not equalize extracted data or routing.
Neutral wording does not repair unequal recommendations or reveal which stage produced them.
Provider evaluations do not measure this application’s corpus, extraction, or routing.

prompt: An eligibility classifier shows equal aggregate error rates across two groups. In one high-stakes region, group A has twice the count of false denials observed for group B, but their eligible-case denominators have not been compared. Which evaluation view is most relevant?

options.text: A larger pooled sample and a single overall accuracy score.
Only the average response time, because model latency can affect group outcomes indirectly.
Compare group-and-region error rates with denominators.
A prompt change applied globally before confirming which stage creates the disparity.

feedback.reason: Compare false-denial rates using eligible-case denominators within each group and region. Twice the count alone does not establish twice the risk.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Fairness checks need outcome-specific slices and may require examination of both model and downstream decision policy.
details.scenarioApplication: Compare false-denial rates using eligible-case denominators within each group and region. Twice the count alone does not establish twice the risk.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Small subgroup estimates may be uncertain; report uncertainty and avoid treating noisy differences as definitive.
details.errorCorrection: Measure comparable cases at the suspected stage; neither a pooled score nor a shared model establishes equal treatment.
details.transfer: Choose metrics that reveal the harm identified by the scenario, not only a global summary.

messages.text: A pooled score can still hide the region-specific false-denial burden.
Latency may merit its own investigation, but cannot replace measuring the false denials already identified.
A global prompt edit chooses a remedy before locating the affected stage or establishing comparable rates.

course.title: Responsible AI, Safety & Risk, Architect Module 3
course.section: M3-S10: Where unequal outcomes enter, and what the system must explain; M3-S11: When fairness is treated as the model provider's problem

prompt: A team changed few-shot examples to improve a task, after which one dialect group receives more low-confidence routes to manual review. The base model did not change. What should the investigator compare?

options.text: The new and old model release notes only; unchanged model identity rules out a model-related cause.
Reviewer volume by week, without comparing the examples used or route decisions.
Only the final approval rates because manual review is outside the AI system.
Compare versioned examples and group-level routing outcomes.

feedback.reason: Few-shot content can alter system behavior; downstream routing is also a point where unequal outcomes can be introduced or amplified.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A versioned before/after comparison helps isolate the change but does not by itself prove causation if traffic or users changed.
details.scenarioApplication: Few-shot content can alter system behavior; downstream routing is also a point where unequal outcomes can be introduced or amplified.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Keep the full decision path measurable and preserve the artifacts needed to reproduce the route.
details.errorCorrection: Measure comparable cases at the suspected stage; neither a pooled score nor a shared model establishes equal treatment.
details.transfer: Inspect changed inputs and downstream actions as part of a fairness investigation.

messages.text: An unchanged base model does not rule out behavior changes caused by new examples.
Total reviewer volume lacks the group-level route and prompt-version links needed to investigate this change.
Manual review is part of the decision path; approval rates alone can hide unequal delay and workload.

course.title: Responsible AI, Safety & Risk, Architect Module 3
course.section: M3-S10: Where unequal outcomes enter, and what the system must explain; M3-S11: When fairness is treated as the model provider's problem

prompt: A document corpus contains far fewer examples from a dialect used in one service region, where quality is lower. There is no immediate safety-stop trigger. To select a targeted quality remedy, which diagnostic step is most defensible?

options.text: Audit corpus and labels; evaluate the affected dialect.
Duplicate the few available examples until group counts match, then assume representation bias is solved.
Raise the confidence threshold globally so uncertain cases across all groups go to review.
Remove the dialect from supported inputs and measure only the remaining population.

feedback.reason: The evidence points to a possible data-coverage issue; diagnose corpus and label quality and measure the affected behavior before selecting a remedy.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Fairness can be affected by corpus representation and the choice of evaluation slice; interventions should respond to measured error modes.
details.scenarioApplication: The evidence points to a possible data-coverage issue; diagnose corpus and label quality and measure the affected behavior before selecting a remedy.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Synthetic or duplicated examples may not capture authentic use, and a global threshold may shift harm to other groups.
details.errorCorrection: Measure comparable cases at the suspected stage; neither a pooled score nor a shared model establishes equal treatment.
details.transfer: Establish trustworthy disaggregated evidence before changing system behavior.

messages.text: Duplicating records changes counts without adding coverage of new dialect forms or correcting bad labels.
A global threshold may shift review burdens across groups without fixing the suspected coverage gap.
Excluding the dialect hides the affected users and does not improve their service quality.

course.title: Responsible AI, Safety & Risk, Architect Module 3
course.section: M3-S10: Where unequal outcomes enter, and what the system must explain; M3-S11: When fairness is treated as the model provider's problem

prompt: A decision-support assistant recommends manual review for 40 of 100 comparable cases in group A and 40 of 1,000 in group B. Labels and sampling have been reviewed, but no stage-level investigation has run. What does this evidence establish?

options.text: Different rates; trace the pipeline before attributing cause.
The route rates are equal because both groups have 40 reviews.
The base model caused discrimination with certainty.
Manual review proves that neither group bears any burden.

feedback.reason: The observed review rates are 40% and 4%. That establishes a routing disparity in this sample, not its cause or whether each review was justified.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Compare outcome rates using their group-specific denominators rather than raw event counts. A tenfold difference in observed manual-review frequency is descriptive evidence; assigning a cause requires tracing input mix, model scores, routing thresholds and reviewer decisions on comparable cases.
details.scenarioApplication: Compute group A's routing rate as `40 / 100 = 40%` and group B's as `40 / 1,000 = 4%`. Preserve group sizes and sampling context, then compare matched case characteristics and per-stage routing events before attributing the difference to the base model, examples or review policy.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Reviewed comparability improves interpretation but does not identify the faulty stage.
details.errorCorrection: Separate the measured disparity, its causal explanation, and the policy used to choose a remedy.
details.transfer: Evaluate comparable outcomes across the full application decision path.

messages.text: Counts use different denominators: 40/100 is 40%, while 40/1,000 is 4%.
The same observation could arise from inputs, examples, thresholds, or routing; stage-level evidence is missing.
Review can protect users while also imposing delay or effort; it is not automatically burden-free.

prompt: Replay of matched cases with frozen inputs, prompt, model, and routing isolates a retrieval defect: the index omitted authoritative documents needed for one dialect. The team repairs indexing. What evidence should precede a claim that this quality gap is fixed?

options.text: Equal document counts in the rebuilt index alone.
A provider statement that the base model passed bias tests.
Retest dialect outcomes and relevant regression slices.
Removal of dialect labels from the evaluation results.

feedback.reason: Retest affected error types and relevant regression slices after repairing retrieval. Index counts alone do not show that users receive correct, supported decisions.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A repaired index is an implementation change, not outcome evidence. Compare retrieval correctness and downstream supported-answer/decision outcomes on the affected dialect and regression slices.
details.scenarioApplication: Use the frozen matched cases that exposed the missing authoritative documents, then rerun the affected dialect and other retrieval-sensitive regression slices and inspect evidence support.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A passing scoped evaluation supports its measured cases; continue monitoring drift rather than claiming universal fairness.
details.errorCorrection: Separate the measured disparity, its causal explanation, and the policy used to choose a remedy.
details.transfer: Evaluate comparable outcomes across the full application decision path.

messages.text: Equal counts do not establish relevant retrieval or correct downstream outcomes.
Provider tests do not verify the repaired application index and decision path.
Removing labels prevents checking the affected slice instead of demonstrating improvement.

course.title: Responsible AI, Safety & Risk, Architect Module 3
course.section: M3-S10: Where unequal outcomes enter, and what the system must explain; M3-S11: When fairness is treated as the model provider's problem

prompt: A pilot routes more cases from one region to human review. The team proposes raising an automatic-approval threshold to equalize route counts. It has not compared error severity, decision accuracy, or waiting time for comparable cases. What should guide the decision?

options.text: Equal route counts alone, regardless of decision quality.
Compare errors, review burdens, and policy trade-offs.
The model’s stated confidence alone, without validation.
The fastest average route, even if serious errors increase.

feedback.reason: Compare errors, their severity, and the burden of review before choosing thresholds. Equal routing counts alone are not a sufficient fairness objective.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Threshold selection changes both decision errors and how often users enter review; those impacts need comparable error and burden measurements plus an accountable policy trade-off.
details.scenarioApplication: Measure severity and accuracy for comparable cases in each region and quantify review wait/workload before adjusting an automatic-approval threshold.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The accountable owner must choose acceptable trade-offs; a threshold cannot make that normative decision by itself.
details.errorCorrection: Separate the measured disparity, its causal explanation, and the policy used to choose a remedy.
details.transfer: Evaluate comparable outcomes across the full application decision path.

messages.text: Equal counts can conceal different populations and error costs; they do not establish comparable treatment.
Unvalidated confidence does not measure decision correctness or the cost imposed on users.
Mean speed does not justify an unexamined increase in consequential errors.
